question: Can fractal pre-training with a small, cheaply generated synthetic budget, chosen by diversity, match or beat fractal pre-training with a larger random budget on a small downstream digit-recognition task?
method: IFS fractal pre-training stand-in for an MLP on sklearn digits; 70/30 stratified split; 20 labelled digits per class for fine-tuning; baseline pre-trains on a random fractal budget, improved pre-trains on the same budget chosen by k-means diversity from a 5x larger pool; seeds 42, 43, 44.

dataset.name: scikit-learn optical recognition of handwritten digits (load_digits)

baseline: MLP (128 hidden units) pre-trained on a random budget of 2000 IFS fractal images labelled by IFS class, then fine-tuned on 200 labelled digits.
improved: Same MLP, same 2000-image budget, but the images are chosen by k-means diversity from a pool of 10000 generated fractal images before identical pre-training and fine-tuning.
notes: Stand-in for the paper's fractal pre-training (not its ViT/CNN); MLPClassifier replaces it. Budget is equal for both methods, so the 'small budget' part of the question is not tested directly. Improved pre-training time includes pool generation and k-means, so it is not a speed-up. k-means on pixels ignores labels, so class balance of the selected set is not enforced. Hyper-parameters were fixed a priori, not tuned. Only 3 seeds and one digit split; the test set was used once at the end.
